text.en: When we don’t know something for sure but conclude it from the signs, we use a modal verb. Must: I am sure it is true (“She must be at home”). Can’t: I am sure it is not true (“That can’t be Carlos”). Might, may, could: it is possible but not certain (“It might rain”). The Spanish “debe de estar”, “tiene que ser” match must be, “no puede ser” matches can’t be, “puede que” matches might / may.
text.es: Cuando no sabemos algo con seguridad pero lo deducimos por las señales, usamos un verbo modal. Must: estoy seguro de que es verdad («She must be at home»). Can’t: estoy seguro de que no es verdad («That can’t be Carlos»). Might, may, could: es posible pero no seguro («It might rain»). El «debe de estar», «tiene que ser» del español equivale a must be, el «no puede ser» a can’t be, el «puede que» a might / may.

text.en: Must / can’t / might + have + participle: a deduction about what happened. After have comes the participle.
text.es: Must / can’t / might + have + participio: una deducción sobre lo que pasó. Después de have va el participio.

text.en: The negative of must for deduction is can’t, not mustn’t. “Her car isn’t here. She can’t be at home.” Mustn’t means a prohibition (“You mustn’t park here”), not a deduction.
text.es: La negación de must en la deducción es can’t, no mustn’t. «Her car isn’t here. She can’t be at home.» Mustn’t significa una prohibición («You mustn’t park here»), no una deducción.

text.en: Must has two meanings: obligation (“You must wear a seat belt”) and deduction (“She must be tired”). The content of the sentence decides which one. For deduction it is usually followed by be, or by have + participle.
text.es: Must tiene dos significados: obligación («You must wear a seat belt») y deducción («She must be tired»). El contenido de la oración decide cuál es. En la deducción suele ir seguido de be, o de have + participio.

text.en: For possibility the Spanish “puede ser” is might / may / could, not can. Say “It could be true” or “It might be true” when you are not sure.
text.es: Para la posibilidad, el «puede ser» español es might / may / could, no can. Di «It could be true» o «It might be true» cuando no estás seguro.

text.en: After a modal verb there is no to and no -s: not “She musts be” and not “It might to rain”. For the past use have + participle: not “must have went” but “must have gone”.
text.es: Después de un verbo modal no hay to ni -s: no «She musts be» ni «It might to rain». Para el pasado se usa have + participio: no «must have went» sino «must have gone».

speak.en: When we don't know something for sure but conclude it, we use a modal verb. «Must» means I am sure it is true: «She must be at home». «Can't» means I am sure it is not true: «That can't be Carlos». «Might», «may» and «could» mean a possibility: «It might rain later». Careful: for deduction the negative of «must» is «can't», not «mustn't». For the past, «must have» plus the participle is used: «Someone must have opened the window».
speak.es: Cuando no sabemos algo con seguridad pero lo deducimos, usamos un verbo modal. «Must» significa que estoy seguro de que es verdad: «She must be at home». «Can't» significa que estoy seguro de que no es verdad: «That can't be Carlos». «Might», «may» y «could» significan una posibilidad: «It might rain later». Cuidado: en la deducción la negación de «must» es «can't», no «mustn't». Para el pasado se usa «must have» más el participio: «Someone must have opened the window».

items.sentence: The lights are on. Ana ___ be at home.

why.en: The light is a sign that she is home; I am sure: Ana must be at home.
why.es: Las luces son una señal de que está en casa; estoy seguro: Ana must be at home.

can't.en: Can’t would mean she is surely not at home; but the light points to the opposite.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no está en casa; pero la luz apunta a lo contrario.

mustn't.en: Mustn’t means a prohibition (she is not allowed to be home), not a deduction.
mustn't.es: Mustn’t significa una prohibición (no se permite que esté en casa), no una deducción.

tr.en: The lights are on. Ana must be at home.
tr.es: Las luces están prendidas. Ana debe estar en casa.

items.sentence: He has been working all day. He ___ be tired.

why.en: He has worked all day; I am sure he is tired: he must be tired.
why.es: Ha trabajado todo el día; estoy seguro de que está cansado: he must be tired.

can't.en: Can’t would mean he is surely not tired; working all day suggests otherwise.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no está cansado; trabajar todo el día sugiere lo contrario.

might to.en: After might there is no to; “might to be” is incorrect and does not express certainty either.
might to.es: Después de might no hay to; «might to be» es incorrecto y tampoco expresa certeza.

tr.en: He has been working all day. He must be tired.
tr.es: Ha estado trabajando todo el día. Debe estar cansado.

items.sentence: That ___ be Carlos. He is in Madrid.

why.en: I am sure it is not him (he is in Madrid): that can’t be Carlos.
why.es: Estoy seguro de que no es él (está en Madrid): that can’t be Carlos.

must.en: Must would mean it is surely Carlos; the second half (he is in Madrid) contradicts that.
must.es: Must significaría que seguro es Carlos; la segunda parte (está en Madrid) lo contradice.

mustn't.en: Mustn’t would be a prohibition; for deduction the negative of must is can’t.
mustn't.es: Mustn’t sería una prohibición; en la deducción la negación de must es can’t.

tr.en: That can't be Carlos. He is in Madrid.
tr.es: Ese no puede ser Carlos. Él está en Madrid.

items.sentence: I am not sure. It ___ rain later.

why.en: I am not sure, it is only possible: it might rain.
why.es: No estoy seguro, solo es posible: it might rain.

must.en: Must would express certainty; “I am not sure” says the opposite.
must.es: Must expresaría certeza; «I am not sure» dice lo contrario.

can't.en: Can’t would mean it surely won’t rain; the sentence is uncertain, so might.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no va a llover; la oración es incierta, por eso might.

tr.en: I am not sure. It might rain later.
tr.es: No estoy seguro. Podría llover más tarde.

items.sentence: Her car isn't here. She ___ be at home.

why.en: Her car is not here; I am sure she is not at home: she can’t be at home.
why.es: Su carro no está aquí; estoy seguro de que no está en casa: she can’t be at home.

mustn't.en: Mustn’t means a prohibition; for deduction the negative of must is can’t.
mustn't.es: Mustn’t significa una prohibición; en la deducción la negación de must es can’t.

doesn't have to.en: Doesn’t have to means it is not required; here you need a deduction.
doesn't have to.es: Doesn’t have to significa que no es obligatorio; aquí hace falta una deducción.

tr.en: Her car isn't here. She can't be at home.
tr.es: Su carro no está aquí. No puede estar en casa.

items.sentence: The window is open. Someone ___ have opened it.

why.en: A deduction about the past: must have + participle (someone surely opened it).
why.es: Una deducción sobre el pasado: must have + participio (alguien seguro la abrió).

can't.en: Can’t have opened would mean nobody opened it; but the window is open.
can't.es: Can’t have opened significaría que nadie la abrió; pero la ventana está abierta.

will.en: Will have does not deduce about the present situation; “will have opened” would mean a future finished event.
will.es: Will have no deduce sobre la situación presente; «will have opened» significaría un hecho futuro terminado.

tr.en: The window is open. Someone must have opened it.
tr.es: La ventana está abierta. Alguien debe haberla abierto.

items.sentence: It ___ have been Ana. She was in Puebla.

why.en: A negative deduction about the past: it can’t have been Ana (she was in Puebla).
why.es: Una deducción negativa sobre el pasado: it can’t have been Ana (estaba en Puebla).

must.en: Must have been would mean it was surely Ana; the second half contradicts that.
must.es: Must have been significaría que seguro fue Ana; la segunda parte lo contradice.

might to.en: After might there is no to, and “might to have” is an incorrect form.
might to.es: Después de might no hay to, y «might to have» es una forma incorrecta.

tr.en: It can't have been Ana. She was in Puebla.
tr.es: No pudo haber sido Ana. Ella estaba en Puebla.

why.en: After must comes the base verb: she must be happy.
why.es: Después de must va el verbo base: she must be happy.

is.en: After a modal verb no conjugated form follows; after must comes be, not is.
is.es: Después de un verbo modal no va una forma conjugada; después de must va be, no is.

being.en: After must comes the base verb, not an -ing form; “must being” is incorrect.
being.es: Después de must viene el verbo base, no una forma -ing; «must being» es incorrecto.

tr.en: She must be very happy.
tr.es: Debe estar muy feliz.

items.sentence: She must have ___ the news. She looks sad.

why.en: After must have comes the participle: must have seen.
why.es: Después de must have va el participio: must have seen.

see.en: “See” is the base verb; after must have you need the participle (seen).
see.es: «See» es el verbo base; después de must have hace falta el participio (seen).

seeing.en: After must have you need the participle, not the -ing form (seen).
seeing.es: Después de must have hace falta el participio, no la forma -ing (seen).

tr.en: She must have seen the news. She looks sad.
tr.es: Debe haber visto las noticias. Se ve triste.

items.sentence: Maria ___ come to the party, but I don't know yet.

why.en: A possibility, not certain: Maria may come.
why.es: Una posibilidad, no segura: Maria may come.

must.en: Must expresses certainty; “I don’t know yet” shows uncertainty.
must.es: Must expresa certeza; «I don’t know yet» muestra incertidumbre.

can't.en: Can’t would mean she surely won’t come; the sentence says I don’t know yet.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no viene; la oración dice que todavía no lo sé.

tr.en: Maria may come to the party, but I don't know yet.
tr.es: Puede que Maria venga a la fiesta, pero aún no lo sé.

items.sentence: I'm not sure where Luis is. He ___ be in the kitchen.

why.en: It is possible but not certain: he could be in the kitchen.
why.es: Es posible pero no seguro: he could be in the kitchen.

must.en: Must would mean certainty; “I’m not sure” expresses uncertainty.
must.es: Must significaría certeza; «I’m not sure» expresa incertidumbre.

can't.en: Can’t would mean he is surely not in the kitchen; the sentence only gives a possibility.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no está en la cocina; la oración solo da una posibilidad.

tr.en: I'm not sure where Luis is. He could be in the kitchen.
tr.es: No estoy seguro de dónde está Luis. Podría estar en la cocina.

why.en: After can’t comes the base verb: that story can’t be true.
why.es: Después de can’t va el verbo base: that story can’t be true.

is.en: After a modal verb no conjugated form follows; after can’t comes be.
is.es: Después de un verbo modal no va una forma conjugada; después de can’t va be.

being.en: After can’t comes the base verb, not an -ing form.
being.es: Después de can’t viene el verbo base, no una forma -ing.

tr.en: That story can't be true.
tr.es: Esa historia no puede ser cierta.

items.sentence: He ___ be hungry. He hasn't eaten all day.

why.en: He has not eaten all day; I am sure he is hungry: he must be hungry.
why.es: No ha comido en todo el día; estoy seguro de que tiene hambre: he must be hungry.

can't.en: Can’t would mean he is surely not hungry; that contradicts the second half.
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no tiene hambre; eso contradice la segunda parte.

might not.en: Might not only gives a possibility that he is not hungry; going all day without food allows a stronger conclusion.
might not.es: Might not solo da la posibilidad de que no tenga hambre; pasar todo el día sin comer permite una conclusión más fuerte.

tr.en: He must be hungry. He hasn't eaten all day.
tr.es: Debe tener hambre. No ha comido en todo el día.

items.sentence: He ___ be a doctor. He knows nothing about medicine.

why.en: I am sure he is not a doctor because he knows nothing about medicine: he can’t be a doctor.
why.es: Estoy seguro de que no es doctor porque no sabe nada de medicina: he can’t be a doctor.

must.en: Must would mean he is surely a doctor; the second half contradicts that.
must.es: Must significaría que seguro es doctor; la segunda parte lo contradice.

mustn't.en: Mustn’t would be a prohibition (he must not be a doctor); for deduction you need can’t.
mustn't.es: Mustn’t sería una prohibición (no debe ser doctor); para la deducción hace falta can’t.

tr.en: He can't be a doctor. He knows nothing about medicine.
tr.es: No puede ser doctor. No sabe nada de medicina.

items.sentence: They are not answering. They ___ be busy.

why.en: A possible explanation, but not certain: they might be busy.
why.es: Una explicación posible, pero no segura: they might be busy.

can't.en: Can’t would mean they are surely not busy; the sentence only sees that nobody answers (they might be busy).
can't.es: Can’t significaría que seguro no están ocupados; la oración solo ve que nadie contesta.

mustn't.en: Mustn’t would be a prohibition (they must not be busy), not a possibility.
mustn't.es: Mustn’t sería una prohibición (no deben estar ocupados), no una posibilidad.

tr.en: They are not answering. They might be busy.
tr.es: No contestan. Podrían estar ocupados.

items.sentence: He ___ have forgotten. He never forgets.

why.en: I am sure he did not forget: he can’t have forgotten.
why.es: Estoy seguro de que no lo olvidó: he can’t have forgotten.

must.en: Must have forgotten would mean he surely forgot; “never forgets” contradicts that.
must.es: Must have forgotten significaría que seguro lo olvidó; «never forgets» lo contradice.

might to.en: After might there is no to; “might to have” is incorrect.
might to.es: Después de might no hay to; «might to have» es incorrecto.

tr.en: He can't have forgotten. He never forgets.
tr.es: No puede haberlo olvidado. Él nunca olvida.

items.sentence: She ___ have left already. Her coat isn't here.

why.en: Her coat is not here; she surely left: she must have left.
why.es: Su abrigo no está aquí; seguro se fue: she must have left.

can't.en: Can’t have left would mean she surely did not leave; the missing coat shows otherwise.
can't.es: Can’t have left significaría que seguro no se fue; el abrigo que falta muestra lo contrario.

will.en: Will have left would mean a future finished event; here you need a deduction about the past (must have).
will.es: Will have left significaría un hecho futuro terminado; aquí hace falta una deducción sobre el pasado (must have).

tr.en: She must have left already. Her coat isn't here.
tr.es: Ya debe haberse ido. Su abrigo no está aquí.
